meta.title: The Noodle Factory in Six Slides
meta.textType: a short story in words and pictures

paragraphs: On Saturday, the Explorers visited a small noodle factory. Mia made a slideshow with six slides. She wrote one short caption under each slide. The slides tell the story of the day. Here they are.

Slide one. At nine o'clock, a man and a woman met the children at the door. They were married, and the factory was their home, too. The door was open, and the smell of warm flour came out. The Explorers took off their shoes at the door. Slide two. The man showed a big machine with a long white table. The man started the machine, and it began to move. The machine can mix flour and water. Then it makes long, thin noodles.

Slide three. Leo looked at the old machine and said, "It is very slow!" The woman looked at her husband, and she did not smile. "That was unkind, Leo," said Teacher Kim quietly. Leo said, "I am sorry." Slide four. Just then, the machine stopped. The man smiled, and he began to repair it. Leo held the light for him. In five minutes, the machine worked again.

Slide five. Then the children mixed flour and water with their hands. The woman gave each child a small bowl of flour and water. Mia's noodles were short and fat, and she laughed. Leo's noodles were long and thin. Slide six. At midday, the Explorers had lunch in the restaurant next door. They ate hot soup with noodles. The bowls were big, and the soup was very hot. Mia took a photo of six empty bowls. "This is the best soup that I have ever eaten," said Leo.

The woman smiled at him and said, "Thank you." "Have you ever made noodles at home?" she asked the children. "No, never," said Mia. "But we want to try now." Lily smiled and said, "A kind word is always better than an unkind word."
text.summary: Mia makes a slideshow of six slides about the Explorers' visit to a small noodle factory. A married couple show the machine, Leo says an unkind thing and says sorry, and the children eat lunch in the restaurant next door.
